Confirming this bug affects **opencode 1.18.10** with MiniMax-M3 (Anthropic-compatible endpoint), and providing empirical data.

## Environment

- **opencode version**: 1.18.10
- **Provider**: `minimax-coding-plan` (uses `https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1`)
- **Model**: `MiniMax-M3` with `variant: thinking`
- **Agent**: `build`
- **Session type**: long-running investigation of legacy codebase

## Empirical data from the affected session

```
Session: ses_064f372afffeAfS6ezjKK9RT5v
Title:   SIPD Convocatorias y Participaciones
Status:  STUCK in compaction loop (process still running, no progress)

Total messages:                 6,483
Total parts (DB rows):           22,837
Total parts size (serialized):   28 MB
Manual compactions performed:    6 (all "auto": false)
Auto compactions triggered:      0
```

### Token breakdown (lifetime totals)

```
tokens_input:       38,391,311
tokens_output:       1,990,637
tokens_cache_read: 1,965,274,137  ← 1.96 BILLION
cost: $0.00
```

### Behavior timeline (last 10 messages, seconds apart)

```
[20:47:40] assistant  in=     693  cr=    133,120  out=     115
[20:47:33] assistant  in=     431  cr=    132,864  out=      82
[20:47:24] assistant  in=     880  cr=    132,224  out=     131
[20:47:10] assistant  in=     579  cr=    131,840  out=     662
[20:46:59] assistant  in=     683  cr=    131,328  out=     386
```

`cache_read` is monotonically growing — each turn re-reads the same context.

### Part distribution (proves the model is in a loop)

```
type=step-start     count=6058
type=step-finish    count=6045
type=tool bash      count=3438
type=text           count=3204
type=reasoning      count=1598
type=tool read      count=1126
type=tool edit      count= 922
...
type=compaction     count=   5  ← ALL manual (auto: false)
```

## Observations consistent with #39291

1. **`auto: true` in compaction config** but **zero auto-compactions ever fired**
2. **Last user prompt is empty** — the model is in inference loop with no new user input
3. **Each turn's `cache_read` keeps growing** — same byte-identical context being re-sent with mutated thinking blocks
4. **6 manual compactions previously succeeded** — but the next turn after each compaction triggered the loop again
5. **Process keeps generating messages** (every ~10 seconds) but makes no progress on actual work

## Compaction config (for reference)

```json
{
  "compaction": {
    "auto": true,
    "prune": true,
    "tail_turns": 2,
    "preserve_recent_tokens": 50000,
    "reserved": 500000
  }
}
```

## Workaround applied

1. `kill -9 <pid>` to stop the looping process
2. **Session is unrecoverable** — opening it again reproduces the same loop
3. New session with same task starts cleanly

## Suggested mitigation for users

Until fixed, disable auto-compaction for sessions using thinking-enabled models:

```json
{
  "compaction": {
    "auto": false   // disable auto-compaction
  }
}
```

Or use a non-thinking variant (`variant: none` or `default`) for long sessions.

## Confirmation

This is **the same** bug as #39291 — auto-compaction with extended thinking enabled produces a request that the API rejects, and opencode retries it forever with the same corrupted payload. The cache_read explosion is the downstream effect of dozens of failed retries per minute over roughly an hour.

Happy to coordinate. Answers in order:

**1. PR target.** I'll base on `2.0` (upstream default), not on `feat/skill-ux-improvements`. Reason: your changes are mostly server-side (`SessionPrompt.prompt` synthetic injection), mine are pure TUI trigger plumbing in `packages/tui/src/prompt/display.ts` + `autocomplete.tsx`. Conflict surface is small, and keeping them independently mergeable means neither PR gets blocked if the other stalls or gets reshaped in review. If yours lands first, mine rebases trivially; if mine lands first, you pick up `tokenTriggerIndex` for free.

**2. `tokenTriggerIndex` refactor.** Yes, opening it as a standalone PR, linked to this issue. It's a pure DRY of `mentionTriggerIndex` with no behavior change on its own; `slashTriggerIndex` + the index-aware `onSelect`/`hide()` work sits on top in the same PR. Reviewer-wise, ping me on yours if you end up adopting the helper, happy to adapt.

**3. Prose ambiguity guards.** Lazy prefix-gating is the clean answer I'd propose: only show the menu if the text after `/` is a prefix of at least one available command. That eliminates false positives from paths, dates, URLs, division, etc. without regex heuristics, because no menu appears unless a real command actually matches. The whitespace-preceded rule stays as a cheap pre-filter; the prefix match is the authoritative gate. If you'd rather handle this server-side as part of the synthetic command expansion, even better, the TUI just stops rendering when the candidate set is empty.

**Split.** To avoid coupling, I'll keep my fork's two changes as separate PRs:
- PR 1 (this issue): mid-line `/` trigger + `tokenTriggerIndex` refactor + tests.
- PR 2 (#35341): the one-line `if (source === "skill") continue` removal, gated on the design questions I left over there. It depends on PR 1's index-aware plumbing for picking a long skill name mid-line.

Next step from me: open PR 1 against `2.0`, link this issue, ping you for review. Sound right?

Update: identified the root cause in my environment.

I was running the official desktop (1.18.10) against a standalone `opencode serve` process (port 15120) started via a systemd user unit. That standalone server did **not** set `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER`, so the working-tree parcel watcher stayed off (it defaults to `false` in `packages/core/src/flag/flag.ts`). The desktop build only enables it when it spawns its own sidecar server (`packages/desktop/src/main/server.ts`), which my standalone server bypassed.

With the working-tree watcher off, external file changes (e.g. `git rm`) produced no `file.watcher.updated` event, so the sidebar never invalidated its vcs diff query until something else forced a refetch (e.g. switching projects).

Fix: set `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER=true` on the standalone server (added it to the systemd unit Environment and restarted). After that, the sidebar and the changes list refresh promptly for both adds and deletes, before and after commit. No code change needed.

Closing as this was an environment/config issue, not a bug.
Closed: root cause was missing OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILEWATCHER on the standalone server, not a code bug.

Thanks for the triage. This issue is distinct from #31870 and #33942, so a clarifying note:

**Scope**: this is specifically the **third-party OpenAI-compatible client** path: Codex CLI (Responses wire) → CLIProxyAPI (OpenAI-compat mode) → Console Go `/chat/completions`. It is not the VS Code extension (#31870) and not the zen/go 500 path (#33942).

**Distinct failure mode**: a standard OpenAI chat completions request with `image_url` content parts is rejected with HTTP 400 **before reaching the model**, via strict serde deserialization:

```
Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[3]: unknown variant `image_url`, expected `text`
```

This is a request-schema rejection (the error echoes the request body), not an upstream model error, and not a 500.

**Why this is effectively the only way to hit it**: opencode CLI stores pasted images as file attachments in the session and never sends `image_url` inline — the model reads them via tools (e.g. the `modlens` skill). So the Console Go endpoint's `image_url` handling can only be exercised by third-party OpenAI-compatible clients, which is exactly this case. The actual upstream model API (DeepSeek official) tolerates image parts ("unsupported but does not error" per its docs), so the rejection is entirely at the Console Go gateway schema layer.

**Minimal ask**: either accept/ignore standard `image_url` content parts (matching upstream model behavior), or at minimum return a proper OpenAI-style error envelope instead of a serde error that echoes the request body, so third-party clients can degrade gracefully instead of failing every request that contains an image (including retries that replay the conversation history).

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:

- #35570: Reports the same `stream()`/`hydrate()` full-session hydration cost in `message-v2.ts`, with near-identical profiling data (197 MB of part JSON, RSS spikes, 3 963 messages → 134 after compaction). That issue focuses on avoiding hydration of discarded compacted parts; this issue adds the complementary root cause that `edit` tool `filediff` metadata is what inflates those parts to begin with.
- #20695: Memory Megathread — the general tracking issue for memory/performance problems across sessions.

If your issue is specifically about the `edit` tool storing full `before`/`after` snapshots (the storage side), it may be worth noting there as a distinct root cause. If it is primarily about the hydration overhead (the load side), #35570 covers that path closely.

Complementary root cause from #40816 (duplicate of this): the `edit` tool's `filediff` metadata is what inflates the historical tool parts in the first place.

**Anatomy of one edit part** (real session, opencode 1.18.13):
```
filediff: { file, before: 214,358 chars, after: 214,698 chars, additions, deletions }
total part JSON: 513,383 bytes   ← ONE small edit to a ~210 KB file
```

The producer at `packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:181` stores the **entire file content twice** (`before` + `after`) in `ctx.metadata({ metadata: { diff, filediff, ... } })` — the compact unified `diff` (a few KB) is also stored, so the two full copies are pure redundancy (the files live on disk + git).

**Real-session totals** (Windows, 1.18.13, two long sessions):

| Session | Messages | Parts | edit parts | edit bytes | Session DB weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (35d) | 7,741 | 31,253 | 1,383 | **194 MB** | 225.8 MB |
| B (25d) | 8,259 | 32,041 | 1,577 | **171.8 MB** | 208.2 MB |

So the hydration cost this issue measures is compounded by storage bloat: ~85% of both sessions' part weight is `edit`-tool full-file snapshots. Even with the two-phase hydration fix, these parts remain in the DB and keep growing (compaction marks but doesn't reclaim them; `compaction.prune` skips the write).

**Proposed storage-side fix** (independent of, and complementary to, the hydration fix): cap or omit `before`/`after` in `filediff` for large files — store only the unified `diff`/`patch` (already present in the same metadata) beyond a size threshold, e.g. skip snapshots for files > 256 KB or truncate to the changed regions. This shrinks the part table ~85% on edit-heavy sessions and reduces the hydration payload even for callers that legitimately need full history.

Validated this fix against two real production sessions (Windows, opencode 1.18.13). The two-phase walk works exactly as proposed — here's the measured impact and one edge case worth deciding on:

## Measured impact (replicated the walk against the live DBs)

| Session | Messages | Parts total | **PR-fix hydrates** | Reduction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (35d, edit-heavy) | 8,010 | 25,659 | **221 msgs / 916 parts** | ~28x |
| B (25d, edit-heavy) | 8,287 | 24,655 | **372 msgs / 1,258 parts** | ~20x |

Both sessions currently hydrate **all** parts on every prompt (`stream()` → `filterCompactedEffect`), which is the observed multi-second block + RSS spike. The row-walk + boundary-stop cuts that to <1,300 parts per prompt.

## One edge case to decide: empty compaction marker behavior

Both sessions carry a compaction part with `tail_start_id: null` (empty marker, 0-char text — they're compaction-managed by a plugin, not opencode's native compaction). In the new walk:

```ts
if (!compaction.tail_start_id) break pages   // ← stops the walk HERE
```

This is a behavior change from the old path: `filterCompacted(stream(...))` with a null `tail_start_id` returned the **full history** (tailIndex = -1 → `return result`), whereas the new walk breaks at the marker and truncates the hydrated set to messages **newer** than it. For the two sessions above that means ~7,800 / ~7,900 older messages become unavailable to the model even though they previously fit (up to the context window). The PR description states "incomplete compactions … unchanged" — this path changes them.

Options:
- **`continue` instead of `break`** on null `tail_start_id` — preserves old behavior for incomplete compactions (no history truncation), at the cost of walking to the session start for those sessions.
- **Keep `break` but document it** — for plugin-compaction-managed sessions (magic-context et al.) the older history is re-injected by the plugin anyway, so the truncation is invisible; but for plain opencode sessions with a stale/failed compaction marker it would silently shorten available history.

Also worth noting: the null-marker case in *old* code already skipped compaction reordering (returned everything), so either choice is defensible — but the "incomplete compactions unchanged" claim in the description only holds with the `continue` variant.

Otherwise the implementation is clean: `messageRows` shares the pagination core with `page()`, the boundary detection correctly keys on `completed` user messages, and the batched hydrate (`rows.slice(index, index + size)`) keeps the fix's memory bounded. LGTM.

Still reproducible on August 6, 2026 with OpenCode Desktop 1.18.x, macOS 26.5.2. Comparative test with other Electron apps installed on the same Mac (VS Code, 1Password, Figma, Dropbox, Miro) confirms the issue is OpenCode-specific — none of them prompt on launch.

**Root cause identified via tccd log capture during launch:**

The log shows OpenCode spawns `ripgrep` (from Homebrew) many times per launch, and each invocation triggers a TCC access check for `kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles`. Every check is denied with:

```
ReqResult(Auth Right: Denied (Service Policy), promptType: 1, DB Action: None)
```

Note **DB Action: None** — meaning the denial is not persisted. Combined with:

```
For ai.opencode.desktop: matches platform requirements: No
```

...this suggests the app's code signature + entitlements combination prevents macOS from caching TCC decisions. Also observed:

```
Prompting policy for hardened runtime; service: kTCCServiceAppleEvents requires entitlement com.apple.security.automation.apple-events but it is missing for responsible={ai.opencode.desktop}
```

**Likely fix on the packaging side:**

1. Add `com.apple.security.automation.apple-events` to the app's entitlements plist so macOS can grant the permission properly.
2. Consider adding `com.apple.security.temporary-exception.files.absolute-path.read-write` for the paths OpenCode actually needs (or drop TCC-triggering paths entirely).
3. Check whether the `ripgrep` spawn pattern is required — hundreds of TCC checks per launch is unusually aggressive.
4. Verify the app is signed with the correct Designated Requirement so cached TCC decisions apply.

Full sample log excerpt available if useful. Happy to test any candidate fix.

While a native mic button is being considered, there's an external option worth knowing about: [qwen-audio-agent](https://github.com/QwenAudio/qwen-audio-agent) connects to OpenCode over ACP (stdio) as a realtime full-duplex voice frontend — click-free push-to-talk isn't needed because it runs always-on with a local wake word and barge-in, on the macOS desktop app, TUI, or web UI. It goes beyond dictation: you speak, the agent works, and you can interrupt it mid-speech. It's listed in the official [ACP clients registry](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/clients).

Disclosure: I'm a maintainer of qwen-audio-agent. Mentioning it because it's a working answer for people who want voice-driven OpenCode today, regardless of whether this feature lands natively.

+1 on the native push-to-talk keybind — the hold-and-release event gap you identified is a real blocker for plugins.

For anyone who wants hands-free OpenCode in the meantime: [qwen-audio-agent](https://github.com/QwenAudio/qwen-audio-agent) runs alongside OpenCode as an ACP client and takes a different approach than push-to-talk — always-on full-duplex voice with a local wake word (sherpa-onnx), barge-in, and voice confirmation for tool calls, so there's no key to hold at all. It covers macOS desktop, TUI, and web.

Disclosure: I'm a maintainer of qwen-audio-agent. This doesn't replace the native feature request — just pointing people at something usable today.
